quote: A word is dead when it is said, some say. I say it just begins to live that day.
source: Emily Dickinson, ‘A word is dead’ (Franklin 278), Poems, Third Series, ed. Mabel Loomis Todd, Life VI (1896)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg 12241, a transcription of Poems by Emily Dickinson, Third Series, edited by Mabel Loomis Todd (Roberts Brothers, 1896).
evidence.edition: Poems by Emily Dickinson, Third Series (Roberts Brothers, 1896)

reason: The 1896 Todd edition prints the six lines exactly as proposed, in section I (Life) as poem VI. Not shipped, not banned, not at cap.
